## Learning Objectives

By the end of this week you should be able to:

1. Represent a graph with an adjacency matrix and a node feature matrix.
2. Explain permutation invariance and equivariance, and why they are required.
3. Derive a graph convolution as neighborhood aggregation.
4. Distinguish node-, edge-, and graph-level prediction tasks.
5. Describe how pooling produces graph-level representations.
6. Implement a GCN layer from the adjacency matrix.
